system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every protective position. Three problems matter most:

1. **The general limitations would apply to everything.** Through the "all Claims of any nature" and "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" wording, the general cap, thresholds and time limits would cover title, capacity and fraud.
2. **The economic terms sit at or beyond our fallbacks.** We have no authority to offer those fallbacks.
3. **The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts its Update.** The Update says Bluefen and Riverlark are "addressed". The Disclosure Letter confirms neither consent, repayment nor discharge has been delivered.

We should reject the package as a basis for agreement and return a mark-up based on our starting positions.

---

## 1. Structural issues (highest priority)

### 1.1 Fraud carve-out is missing, and limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Departure:** As drafted, the caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance would bar or limit claims for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct.
- **Why it matters:** This is a non-negotiable playbook position, and no one on the team can waive it. Some fraud protection may survive at law regardless, but we should not rely on that.
- **Push back:** Insert an express carve-out. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be excluded from all caps, baskets, de minimis, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable.

### 1.2 Hidden general-regime override (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Departure:** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." This defaults every limitation onto every category, including Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenant claims. A single drafting omission anywhere would therefore cut against us.
- **Push back:** Delete it. Each limitation must state expressly which category it applies to (general Warranty Claims only). Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnity, payment and covenant regimes must stay separate.

### 1.3 Title and capacity folded into the general regime
- **Departure:** "Administrative simplicity" would put title at a 20% cap and 18 months. We are paying AUD 24m for the shares. If title fails, our loss is the whole price.
- **Push back:** Keep a separate Fundamental regime with:
  - a 100% cap (AUD 24,000,000);
  - a claims period of at least six years;
  - no basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.

---

## 2. Economic limitation terms

| Term | Seller | Playbook | Position |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m | **Reject.** 20% is a conditional fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority for this specific draft. None has been given, so we must not concede or signal it. |
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject: 5x our position. |
| Basket | AUD 250,000, deductible (excess only) | AUD 50,000, tipping (first dollar) | Reject on both amount and mechanism. Together these terms would leave the first AUD 250k of loss permanently unrecoverable. |
| General claims period | 18 months | 24 months | **Reject.** 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. |

**Process point:** The Seller has opened at exactly our two authority-gated fallbacks (20% and 18 months). We should not treat this as a sign the gap is narrow. If the team thinks a move may be needed later, it should be escalated to Amelia Frost for written authority before anything is said to the Seller.

---

## 3. Disclosure and knowledge

### 3.1 General disclosure (DL 1.1, 1.2)
- **Departure:** The letter deems disclosed the whole data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records". This would quietly wipe out much of the warranty protection.
- **Push back:** Delete paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2. Only specific disclosures should count, made with enough detail for the Buyer to fairly identify the nature and scope of the matter. Data-room documents should be disclosed only where a specific disclosure cross-refers to them.
- **Also:** Paragraph 1.4 (no admission) is acceptable in principle. It must not, however, operate to dilute the effect of the specific disclosures.

### 3.2 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- **Departure:** This is a blanket exclusion covering the Buyer's and its advisers' knowledge, extended to anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. That reintroduces deemed disclosure by another route.
- **Push back:** Delete it.
- Any knowledge qualifier must be limited to named Seller knowledge persons who have made reasonable enquiry.
- Buyer knowledge must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

---

## 4. Specific transaction matters

### 4.1 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3; DL 2)
- **Risk:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30%, of FY26 revenue, and its contract has a change-control clause (11.2) with conditions (11.3).
- **Problems:**
  - The Update calls the matter "addressed", but DL 2 confirms there is no final consent and no evidence the conditions are satisfied.
  - "Satisfied on delivery" of a consent letter ignores whether the 11.3 conditions are met.
  - "Reasonable endeavours" alone is insufficient for a customer of this size.
- **Push back:** Make it a condition precedent to Completion that we receive both:
  - an effective written Bluefen consent; and
  - evidence satisfactory to the Buyer that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.

  Back this with a Buyer walk-right if it is not satisfied, and with a stronger endeavours obligation on the Seller.

### 4.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7; DL 3)
- **Risk:** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, with change-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions. DL 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge exists. A release "following Completion" would leave us owning a company whose assets may be encumbered and whose facility may be in default.
- **Push back:** Require all of the following:
  - a current payout letter;
  - repayment directly from Completion funds, as a funds-flow line item;
  - effective security releases delivered at Completion;
  - PPSR discharges to follow.
- **Limits:** A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither currently exists.
- **Price mechanics:** Repayment should come out of the debt-free price, not on top of it.

### 4.3 Employee closing bonuses (Funds flow; DL 5)
- **Departure:** The AUD 420,000 in DD-005 bonuses is described as "a matter for the Seller" yet is excluded from the funds flow. The bonuses are presumably Company obligations triggered by Completion. Payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are not addressed. The funds flow is therefore silently excluding them, which our playbook prohibits.
- **Push back:** Add a specific funds-flow line item, or treat the bonuses as Debt/Transaction Costs deducted from price. Include all triggered on-costs and PAYG withholding. Back this with an indemnity covering any shortfall.

### 4.4 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4)
- **Departure:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment. Under DD-004 cl 7.3, however, the transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or validly use the Ironquay deliverables. This includes third-party claims, re-development costs and any amounts payable to Ironquay.
  - Preserve a cure route: payment of the outstanding SOW3 fees plus delivery of a confirmatory assignment, preferably as a pre-Completion deliverable.
- **Caveat:** The AUD 180,000 open in DD-010 is not independently verified, either as unpaid or as paid. We should not draft or negotiate on the basis that it is a confirmed debt or a confirmed nil.

### 4.5 Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DL 6)
- **Departure:** The Seller's statement that the matter is "not expected to be material" goes beyond its own disclosure. DL 6 says access, scope and notification duty are all unestablished and the investigation is preliminary.
- **Our stance:** We also should not assert a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or dollar figure.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete the materiality characterisation.
  - Add covenants to preserve logs, complete the investigation (ideally forensically) and give the Buyer regular updates and access before Completion.
  - Require the Seller to make any notification decision in consultation with the Buyer.
  - Consider a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident. It should not be subject to the general limitations or to disclosure of DD-006.

### 4.6 Sandbar renewals (DL 8)
- **Facts:** There are three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total). The Seller calls them "ordinary course", but its own disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Our stance:** Do not accept the Seller's label. We also should not automatically classify the renewals as Debt or deduct them from price.
- **Push back:**
  - Seek the contracts and the commercial rationale for the renewals.
  - Ask why they were renewed together close to sale.
  - Ask whether they can be terminated and how much has been prepaid or accrued.
  - Pending that assessment, add a covenant prohibiting further renewals or commitments of this kind before Completion without Buyer consent.

### 4.7 Tax and IP warranties
- **Departure:** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime". They are not settled. They remain **open** under our playbook.
- **Push back:** Record them as open in the issues list and keep them separate from the general regime. Do not let the "general regime" framing (or the cl 12.3 override) resolve them by default. Equally, we should not assert that unlimited liability has been agreed.

### 4.8 Title evidence (DL 10)
- **Departure:** DD-012 is the Company's own internal share register, supplied by the Seller. It is not independent proof, and DL 10 itself concedes we have not verified it.
- **Push back:** Require independent evidence, including:
  - an ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
  - share issue and transfer history, with stamping or board approvals as relevant;
  - PPSR searches over Harbourglass and the shares;
  - evidence of Harbourglass's authority and capacity to sell (constitution, board resolution);
  - confirmation of no pre-emptive rights, options or encumbrances;
  - full title warranties under the Fundamental regime (see 1.3).

### 4.9 Lower-priority points to verify
- **Office lease (DD-007):** The disclosure says only a notification is required. We should confirm by reading the lease and include the notice in the Completion deliverables.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** The disclosure says there is an assignment restriction only, with no change-of-control trigger. We should confirm against the contract text.
- These are not pushback points yet, but we should not rely on the Seller's characterisation alone.

---

## 5. General observations
- **Stale disclosure:** The disclosure is made as at 22 September 2026, which is about six weeks old. We should require:
  - an updated disclosure position;
  - warranties repeated at Completion;
  - a Buyer right to terminate if anything material arises between signing and Completion.
- **Inconsistent characterisations:** The Update's characterisations ("addressed", "adequate", "not expected to be material", "ordinary course", "settled") do not match the facts in the Seller's own Disclosure Letter. We should point this out politely in the cover note, and our mark-up should rely on the disclosed facts rather than the Seller's labels.

---

## 6. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Recommendation | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct | Carve out of all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. Non-waivable. | Critical |
| 2 | "Applies to all Claims" override | Delete. Limitations apply expressly to general Warranty Claims only. | Critical |
| 3 | Title/capacity | Separate Fundamental regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, no basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Critical |
| 4 | Title evidence | Independent ASIC, PPSR and authority evidence. DD-012 is insufficient. | Critical |
| 5 | Bluefen | CP requiring effective consent **and** evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours alone. | Critical |
| 6 | Riverlark | Payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion. No post-completion release without an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval. | Critical |
| 7 | General cap | Hold at 25% / AUD 6m. No authority for 20%. | High |
| 8 | Thresholds | AUD 5k de minimis; AUD 50k tipping basket | High |
| 9 | Claims period | 24 months. No authority for 18. | High |
| 10 | Disclosure | Delete general / data-room / public-register disclosure. Specific fair disclosure only. | High |
| 11 | Buyer knowledge | Delete cl 8.3. Any qualifier limited to named Seller persons + reasonable enquiry, never applying to title, capacity, fraud or indemnities. | High |
| 12 | Bonuses | AUD 420k plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or price deduction, with an indemnity | High |
| 13 | Ironquay | Broaden the indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure. Treat AUD 180k as unverified. | High |
| 14 | DD-006 incident | Delete the "not material" wording. Add preservation, investigation and update covenants. Consider a specific indemnity. Assert no breach or figure. | High |
| 15 | Tax / IP | Record as OPEN, separate from the general regime. Not settled. | High |
| 16 | Sandbar | Assess, and impose a pre-Completion covenant. No automatic Debt treatment or deduction. | Medium |
| 17 | Lease / Mossvale | Verify against source contracts | Low |
| 18 | Bring-down | Updated disclosure and repetition of warranties at Completion | Medium |

**Internal action:** If the deal team expects to need movement on the cap (20%), the claims period (18 months) or a post-completion Riverlark release, seek Amelia Frost's written authority referencing this draft **before** any concession is signalled. Until then, our mark-up should reflect starting positions only.
=== END ADVICE ===
